source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Which EARLY sign of leprosy does Mang Isko show?
questions.rationale: Early signs include skin color change, loss of sensation, less sweating and hair over the lesion, and thickened, painful nerves. Madarosis, clawing, and a sunken nose bridge are late signs.
questions.quote: Loss of sensation on the skin/Anesthesia

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Mang Isko is classified as multibacillary. Which MDT regimen will he receive?
questions.rationale: Multibacillary (infectious) leprosy is treated with rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone for 12 months. Paucibacillary leprosy uses rifampicin and dapsone for 6–9 months.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Mang Isko has an anesthetic foot. What should the nurse teach him?
options: Test bath water before stepping in
Soak feet in hot water daily
Put full weight on the foot
questions.rationale: With an anesthetized limb, the client avoids injury by not overloading it, testing water before entering to prevent scalds, and wearing proper footwear.
questions.quote: testing water before entering to prevent scalding, and wearing appropriate footwear.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with leprosy cannot close his eyelids completely. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Lagophthalmos, the inability to close the eyelids, is a late sign. The client uses a tear substitute and protects the eyes to prevent corneal ulceration.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Which condition does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Scabies causes intense itching that worsens at night, with burrows in the finger webs, wrists, and elbows.
questions.quote: Intense itching that becomes more severe at night

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Who should be treated for scabies in this case?
questions.rationale: All household members, including close contacts, should be treated to prevent reinfestation.
questions.quote: All members of the household, including close contact should be treated

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Permethrin cream is prescribed. How long should it stay on the skin?
questions.rationale: Permethrin cream is left on the skin for 8 to 12 hours. Fingernails are cut short and contaminated linens are boiled or dry-cleaned.
questions.quote: Permethrin derma cream left on the skin for 8-12 hours

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child has a mild rash, low fever, and postauricular lymph nodes. The nurse sees pinkish spots on the soft palate. What are these?
questions.rationale: Forchheimer spots, a pinkish rash on the soft palate, appear in rubella (German measles), along with postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)
questions.quote: Forchheimer’s spot (pinkish rash on the soft palate)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is rubella especially dangerous for pregnant women?
options: It is teratogenic to the fetus
questions.rationale: Rubella is teratogenic. Congenital rubella can cause cataracts, deafness, heart defects such as PDA, microcephaly, and intellectual disability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)
questions.quote: It has a teratogenic effect on the fetus.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which classic finding of congenital rubella syndrome affects the skin?
questions.rationale: Classic congenital rubella syndrome includes growth retardation, low birth weight, and thrombocytopenic purpura known as 'blueberry muffin' skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)
questions.quote: Thrombocytopenic purpura known as “blueberry muffin” skin

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where are head lice and nits MOST commonly found?
questions.rationale: Head lice and nits are most commonly found behind the ears and on the hair of the neck and occiput.
questions.quote: Head lice and their nits are most commonly found behind the ears and on the hairs of the neck and occiput.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How should a family prevent head lice reinfestation?
questions.rationale: Clothes and bed linens are washed in hot water, ironed, or dry-cleaned to prevent reinfestation.
questions.quote: Clothes and bed linens must be washed in hot water, ironed or dry cleaned.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of herpes zoster (shingles)?
questions.rationale: Herpes zoster is reactivated varicella in the dorsal root ganglia. It causes unilateral, segmental, painful lesions, usually on the trunk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herpes Zoster (PDF p. 152)
questions.quote: It is acute unilateral and segmented inflammation of the dorsal root ganglia

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Dodong, 4, unvaccinated, has a sore throat, low fever, and a swollen neck.
questions.stem: The nurse sees a grayish membrane on Dodong's tonsils. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Diphtheria forms a grayish pseudomembrane and may cause bull neck, a swelling of the soft tissues of the neck.
questions.quote: Exudates forming the membrane are grayish in appearance (Pseudomembrane)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Dodong, 4, unvaccinated, has a sore throat, low fever, and a swollen neck.
questions.stem: Which type of diphtheria is MOST fatal in children aged 2 to 5?
questions.rationale: Laryngeal diphtheria is most common in ages 2 to 5 and the most fatal because of airway anatomy. The voice becomes hoarse and is finally lost.
questions.quote: It is considered as most severe and more fatal type due to anatomical reason

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child's Schick test shows induration at the injection site. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: A positive Schick test (inflammation or induration) means the person lacks antibodies to diphtheria and is susceptible.
questions.quote: This indicates that the client lacks antibodies to diphtheria.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which nursing care is appropriate for a child with diphtheria?
questions.rationale: Care includes absolute bed rest for at least two weeks (to protect the heart from myocarditis), a soft diet with small frequent feedings, and an ice collar to the neck.
questions.quote: Absolute bed rest for at least two weeks

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the MOST dangerous complication of pertussis?
questions.rationale: Bronchopneumonia is the most dangerous complication of pertussis. Others include convulsions, otitis media, hernia, and malnutrition.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which equipment must be at the bedside of an infant with pertussis?
questions.rationale: Suction equipment should be at the bedside to clear thick secretions during paroxysms.
questions.quote: Suction Equipment should be present at bedside
